chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from a man, from Salma the seller of caps, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) entered upon him. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'O my son! Will you not purify your shirt?' So he went, and we thought that something had touched his garment. So he returned and said: 'It is like this.' So we said: 'May Allah make us your ransom, what is the matter with his shirt?' He said: 'His shirt was long, and I instructed him to shorten it.'
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'And your garments, purify.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling regarding the length of garments based on the Quranic verse 'And your garments, purify'?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of the Quranic command to purify one's garments by linking physical cleanliness with the aesthetic and functional practice of shortening long robes, a common custom of the time. It highlights the Imam’s attention to detail in maintaining ritual purity (*taharah*) through everyday attire, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between outward appearance and inner spiritual cleanliness. The narration serves as a foundational text for the jurisprudence of dress, emphasizing that garments should be kept free from dirt and impurity to ensure validity of prayer and general worship.
